provenance.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a polished warm dimensional children book production reference titled "Lilia — 24 studies" on ivory, FOUR rows of SIX readable cells with generous margins. Subject: Elderly female squirrel forest wizard, HUGE round glass spectacles; original chapter30 blocks3–7 and chapter31 block2. Proposed warm adaptation: muted russet silver-tipped fur, cream face/belly, fluffy silver-gray curved tail. No wizard hat or human body. Source distinction: Original magical squirrel image provides scene context but lacks the text-required spectacles and does not prove a named portrait. Spectacles/elderly female squirrel are textual facts; adapted facial design proposed. Input1 subject source/context only; input2 PinPin sheet is LAYOUT/DIRECTION ONLY, never copy hedgehog species, anatomy or clothing; input3 family is lighting/render style only. One subject per cell. Row1 FACE VIEWS: Front: nose/beak centered toward viewer. Left 3/4: nose/beak points SCREEN LEFT, both eyes visible, torso turned LEFT. Left profile: true side, nose/beak points SCREEN LEFT, torso LEFT. Right 3/4: nose/beak points SCREEN RIGHT, both eyes visible, torso turned RIGHT. Right profile: true side, nose/beak points SCREEN RIGHT, torso RIGHT. Rear: back of head/body, face invisible. Row2 EXPRESSIONS: Calm, Curious, Happy, Surprised, Thoughtful, Mild upset, naturally varied eyebrows/mouths. Row3 WHOLE BODY VIEWS explicitly: Front: nose/beak centered toward viewer. Left 3/4: nose/beak points SCREEN LEFT, both eyes visible, torso turned LEFT. Left profile: true side, nose/beak points SCREEN LEFT, torso LEFT. Right 3/4: nose/beak points SCREEN RIGHT, both eyes visible, torso turned RIGHT. Right profile: true side, nose/beak points SCREEN RIGHT, torso RIGHT. Rear: back of head/body, face invisible. Whole tails/feet visible, grounded and consistently scaled within row. Row4 NORMAL POSES: Sit, Reach, Greet, Carry small nut, Share, Rest; birds instead Perch, Hop, Sing, Spread wings, Bathe, Rest, bird anatomy only. Clear concise labels and section divisions, complete bodies, distinct limbs and support; no fused paws, no cropped heads/tails. Keep readable friendly staging for four-year-olds. Do not print invented ages, heights or names. One unified actual image.

SIX readable large panels, THREE rows of TWO, full bodies/tails/feet, generous margins and short action labels, ivory background, warm dimensional PinPin style. Input references in order: 1 PRIMARY-target-solo, 2 subject-source:original-visual-context, 3 counterpart:pinpin, 4 counterpart:tutu, 5 book-style-and-family-scale. FIRST image is PRIMARY working target identity; lock target species, facial design, colors, anatomy in EVERY panel. Counterpart sheets are identity only; do not copy their grid into panels. Family Mama copper-quilled adult left, Papa broader cooler-quilled adult center, PinPin older child right; infant excluded. Source/proposal distinction: Original magical squirrel image provides scene context but lacks the text-required spectacles and does not prove a named portrait. Spectacles/elderly female squirrel are textual facts; adapted facial design proposed.. Target facts: Elderly female squirrel forest wizard, HUGE round glass spectacles; original chapter30 blocks3–7 and chapter31 block2. No merged bodies, duplicate paws/wings, unsupported children or cropped tails.
